newsitem.title: LATVIA: SHELL PLANS MORE EXPANSION IN BALTICS.
newsitem.headline: SHELL PLANS MORE EXPANSION IN BALTICS.

text.p: Oil giant Shell is planning to open more service stations in the Baltic states in 1997 as it keeps up its pace of expansion in the three countries, Shell-Latvija general director Pedro Cardenes said on Friday.
He told Reuters in a recent interview that Shell had 24 filling stations in the Baltics, 14 of which opened in 1996.
"We would like to maintain this pace for the next two years," Cardenes said.
He said the company planned to open 12 stations in 1997 and 12 in 1998.
Cardenes said that Shell's major competitors in the Baltics were Statoil and Neste.
Statoil had around 11 to 12 percent market share while Neste was at around eight to nine percent, he added. The Shell market share was some 4.5 percent in all three Baltic states.
But Cardenes said that in total Western companies had just 25 percent of the market, with local large chains and one-man operations accounting for the remaining three quarters.
"We are catching up but we need to accelerate," Cardenes said of Shell's competition with Neste and Shell.

Cardenes said that Shell would prefer to source its product supplies from eastern Europe as this would mean a 10 to 15 percent cost saving but that the necesary quality and reliable delivery could not yet be guaranteed.
